title: Company-wide policies and processes: Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendor, Travel, Templates
author: Aisha Grant
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and the canonical internal templates. It is intended for all employees, hiring managers, and team leads. Teams must follow these processes; deviations require an approved exception (see "Risk & Exceptions" process in Security).

Scope and applicability

- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors with access to company systems or data.
- Covers corporate (Gmail, GSuite, Slack), infra (cloud accounts, clusters), and product-level systems (APIs, model-serving platforms).
- Does not replace team-specific runbooks; it sets the organizational baseline and mandatory controls.

Ownership and escalation

- Primary owner: People Ops (policy stewardship, access lifecycle coordination).
- Security: IAM, data classification, privileged access reviews.
- Finance & Legal: procurement, vendor contracting, expense policy enforcement.
- Platform/Infra: technical change approvals, rollout coordination.
- Escalation path: team lead -> functional owner -> People Ops -> CTO (for unresolved or high-risk issues).

1) Access and permissions

Principles

- Least privilege by default: grant only the permissions required to complete a job.
- Role-based access control (RBAC) where supported; use groups rather than individual grants.
- Time-bound elevated access for break-glass or privileged tasks with audit logging.

Onboarding checklist (minimum)

1. Create corporate account (People Ops)
2. Add to Slack and team channels (People Ops)
3. Add to GitHub/GitLab team (Engineering manager)
4. Request environment access via Access Request Portal (see links) with justification and expiration date (requester)
5. Confirm MFA and device enrollment (user/Security)

Offboarding checklist (minimum)

1. Disable SSO/Credentials (People Ops)
2. Revoke cloud console access and remove from groups (Infra/Platform)
3. Transfer ownership of tickets/repos (Manager)
4. Update vendor/contract records if applicable (Finance & Legal)

Privilege elevation process

- All elevation requests must be submitted through the Access Request Portal and include: justification, duration (max 7 days for standard requests), approver (service owner), and rollback plan.
- Emergency access ("break-glass") is allowed with mandatory post-fact audit and a required incident ticket within 24 hours.

Access review cadence

- Quarterly automated group membership reviews (People Ops + Security).
- Annual privileged account attestation process (Team owners).

2) Change management

Goal: safe, auditable changes with minimal disruption.

Change categories and required approvals (summary table)

| Change type | Risk level | Required approvers | Window | Rollback required |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| Config change (non-prod) | Low | Service owner | Anytime | Optional |
| Config change (prod) | Medium | Service owner + Platform reviewer | Maintenance window | Yes |
| Infra change (cluster/VM/DB) | High | Eng Platform + Security + Owner | Pre-scheduled window | Yes |
| Emergency/security fix | High | On-call + Security | ASAP | Post-deploy rollback plan |

Standard change process (recommended)

1. Create a Change Request (CR) in the Change Management system with description, impact, test plan, and rollback plan.
2. Assign reviewers: service owner, platform, and security for high-risk items.
3. Schedule deployment in an approved change window (see calendar) and notify stakeholders.
4. Execute and monitor; collect post-change metrics and update CR.
5. Perform post-change review and close CR.

Emergency change handling

- Use the Emergency Change workflow in the on-call playbook.
- Emergency changes must be logged within 2 hours and reviewed in the next change review board (CRB) meeting.

Change blackout windows

- Critical business blackout: end-of-quarter reconciliation windows (finance) — no non-emergency changes permitted.
- Public launch windows — changes restricted per product launch checklist.

3) Data management

Data classification (three tiers)

| Classification | Description | Handling requirements |
|---|---|---|
| Public | Information intended for public consumption | No special controls |
| Internal | Company-internal operational data | SSO protected, standard backups |
| Restricted (PII / Customer-sensitive) | Personal data, customer data, regulated datasets | Encryption at rest & in transit, limited access, logging, retention policy |

Data handling requirements

- All Restricted data must be stored in approved enclaves (private deployment or VPC-hosted buckets) with KMS-managed keys.
- Do not copy Restricted data to third-party services unless covered by a Data Processing Agreement and approved by Legal.
- Mask or redact PII in logs; enable structured logging filters.

Retention and deletion

- Default retention: Internal = 3 years, Restricted = retention as per contract or regulation (documented per dataset).
- Deletion requests: data subject or internal retention change requests follow the Data Deletion Request form; Security & Legal validate and execute.

Backups and recovery

- Critical production systems: daily backups with 30-day rolling retention; quarterly snapshots kept for 1 year for critical financial datasets.
- Restore drills: at least biannual DR exercises for core services (Platform & SRE).

Data access request process

1. Requestor submits Data Access Request with purpose, dataset, and duration.
2. Data owner and Security review for least-privilege and approve/deny.
3. Approved requests are given time-bound access and logged.

4) Procurement & expenses

Procurement flow (summary)

- Low-value purchases (<= $5,000): Requestor creates an Expense Request in Concur/Expense tool; manager approval required.
- Medium purchases ($5,001 - $50,000): Purchase Order (PO) required; Procurement team validates vendor and terms, Finance approves budget.
- High-value purchases (> $50,000): Procurement + Finance + Legal review; executive sponsor required.

Approval thresholds (table)

| Amount | Required approvals |
|---:|---|
| Up to $5,000 | Manager approval |
| $5,001 - $50,000 | Manager + Procurement |
| > $50,000 | Manager + Procurement + Finance + Legal + Executive sponsor |

Corporate card policy

- Corporate cards are issued by Finance following manager nomination. Cards are for approved business expenses only.
- Monthly reconciliation required within 10 business days of statement close. Personal charges must be reimbursed and reported.

Expense reimbursement rules

- Receipts required for all expenses > $25.
- Per diem caps for meals per region (see Expense Templates).
- Non-compliance may result in suspension of card privileges.

Vendor onboarding and contracting (summary)

- Vendors must be evaluated for security posture, data handling, and financial stability.
- For vendors handling Restricted data: require Data Processing Agreement and Security Assessment.
- Contract checklist: scope, SLAs, liability caps, termination, data ownership, and audit rights.

5) Vendor management

Vendor risk assessment steps

1. Initial vendor intake form (requestor) with business justification.
2. Security questionnaire (filled by vendor) and review by Security.
3. Legal review and contract negotiation.
4. Procurement issues PO and creates vendor record.

Vendor monitoring and SLAs

- Critical vendors (infrastructure, model providers, core services) have quarterly SLA reviews and a designated account owner.
- Maintain a vendor inventory with contract end dates and renewal reminders (Procurement).

Termination and offboarding

- Ensure data return/destruction clauses are executed.
- Revoke all credentials and API keys; confirm with Security and Platform.

6) Travel policy (business travel and reimbursement)

Booking and approvals

- All travel must be approved by the traveler’s manager and booked through the corporate travel portal where available.
- Economy class for flights under 6 hours; premium economy may be approved for flights > 6 hours with manager sign-off.

Expense caps and per diems (examples)

- Domestic meal cap: $75/day.
- International meal cap: varies by region; refer to Expense Templates.
- Hotel: reasonable economy or business class; avoid luxury properties unless pre-approved.

Safety and compliance

- Travelers must register trips with Travel & Safety vendor (contact in Appendix).
- Follow local guidance for visas and health requirements.

7) Internal templates and artifacts

Canonical templates (stored in Templates folder)

- Expense report template (Concur)
- Purchase request / PO template
- Vendor security questionnaire (PDF/Doc)
- Access Request form (Access Request Portal link)
- Change Request (CR) template with fields: description, risk, test plan, rollback plan, approvers
- Data Deletion Request template

How to request an exception

- Exceptions to any policy must be submitted via the Policy Exception Request form and include rationale, compensating controls, and duration. Security, People Ops, and the policy owner must approve.

Appendix: quick reference tables

Approval contacts

- People Ops (policy owner): people-ops@redwood.ai
- Security (IAM & data): iam-security@redwood.ai
- Procurement & Finance: procurement@redwood.ai, finance@redwood.ai
- Platform/Infra: platform-oncall@redwood.ai
